subject: mathematics
question_text: If the matrix with rows (0, 4, −2), (−4, 0, 8) and (2, −8, x) is skew symmetric, find the value of x.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.34, chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 16. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards setting up the condition Aᵀ = −A separately from solving the one equation it leaves, because a student who writes only x = 0 has shown no method. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Related card in the same unit: ts_ipe_m1a_mat_vsaq_skew_symmetric_find_x puts the unknown in an OFF-diagonal position, where the answer comes from the sign flip; here the unknown sits ON the diagonal, where the answer is forced to be 0. The two are separate questions and the contrast is worth keeping.

recall_prompt: Say what condition skew symmetry gives, and how it fixes x here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write Aᵀ and set Aᵀ = −A
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write both matrices out. Every entry off the diagonal already agrees, which is the check that the question is consistent.
lines: A is skew symmetric means Aᵀ = −A.
Off the diagonal the entries already match:

recall.must_convey: That the condition is Aᵀ = −A, and that writing both matrices out shows every off-diagonal entry already agreeing.
accept: skew symmetric means A transpose equals minus A
write the transpose and write minus A and compare them
all the off diagonal entries already match
A transpose equals minus A ani rasi, entries compare cheyyali
the two matrices agree everywhere except the last diagonal entry

steps.why: Setting Aᵀ = −A turns the word skew symmetric into nine ordinary equations between numbers. Eight of them are already true, so writing them out shows the question is consistent and points at the only one that is not.
common_mistakes: Using Aᵀ = A, which is the symmetric condition.
Transposing only part of the matrix.
Changing the sign of A but forgetting to change the sign of x.
steps.memory_tip: Skew symmetric means transpose it, then flip every sign, and get the same matrix back.

steps.label: Solve the diagonal entry
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Only the (3,3) entries are left: x on one side, −x on the other. That gives 2x = 0 and x = 0.
lines: This agrees with the general rule that every
diagonal entry of a skew symmetric matrix is 0.

recall.must_convey: That the (3,3) entry gives x = −x, so 2x = 0 and x = 0.
accept: x equals minus x so two x is zero and x is zero
the diagonal entry must be its own negative so it is zero
every diagonal entry of a skew symmetric matrix is zero so x is zero
x equals minus x kabatti x zero
the answer is x equals zero

steps.why: A diagonal entry is its own mirror image, so skew symmetry asks it to equal its own negative. The only number that does that is zero, which is why no skew symmetric matrix can carry a non-zero diagonal entry.
common_mistakes: Answering x = 8 or x = −8 by pairing x with an off-diagonal entry.
Answering x = 2 by copying the (3,1) entry.
steps.memory_tip: On the diagonal skew symmetry says x = −x, and only 0 satisfies that.
